title: Memory for an Unfinished Task
section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
transcript:
Imagine leaving an essay halfway through a paragraph. Hours later, the unfinished sentence may return to your mind while you are doing something unrelated. Psychologists have suggested that incomplete goals remain mentally active, but this idea can be difficult to separate from a simpler explanation: perhaps unfinished work is remembered because it is worrying.

To examine the distinction, a lecturer described an experiment involving a set of short puzzles. Participants worked on some puzzles until completion and were interrupted during others. Before leaving the laboratory, half the participants wrote down a specific plan for finishing each interrupted puzzle. The remainder wrote a description of the room. Both groups were told that they could return the next day, so the opportunity to continue was the same.

Later, while participants performed an unrelated reading task, they occasionally reported thoughts about the unfinished puzzles. Such thoughts occurred less frequently among those who had made a plan. However, when asked directly to identify the puzzles they had encountered, these participants remembered them just as well as the other group. Planning seemed to reduce spontaneous reminders without erasing the memory of the task.

The lecturer cautioned against interpreting the finding as proof that every interruption is harmless. The puzzles were brief, participation was voluntary, and no one faced an examination deadline. A difficult personal obligation may remain distracting even after a plan has been written.

Nevertheless, the study suggests a useful distinction between storing a goal and repeatedly bringing it to attention. An effective plan may reassure the mind that a task has a place in the future. This could explain why a precise next step is sometimes more calming than a general intention to work harder.

questions.prompt: What alternative explanation for remembering unfinished work is mentioned?
options: The work is always more enjoyable.
People remember it because it causes concern.
People are tested on unfinished work more often.
questions.answer: People remember it because it causes concern.
questions.explanation: 开头提出另一种解释：未完成工作使人担心，所以更容易反复想起。

questions.prompt: What differed between the two groups before they left the laboratory?
options: Whether they could return the following day.
Whether their puzzles had written instructions.
Whether they made a specific plan for unfinished puzzles.
Whether they were allowed to complete any puzzles.
questions.answer: Whether they made a specific plan for unfinished puzzles.
questions.explanation: 一组为未完成谜题写具体计划，另一组描写房间；次日返回机会相同。

questions.prompt: What happened to participants who made a plan?
options: They had fewer spontaneous reminders but retained their memories.
They found the reading task impossible to finish.
They remembered only the puzzles they had completed.
questions.answer: They had fewer spontaneous reminders but retained their memories.
questions.explanation: 写计划减少了无意识想起谜题的次数，但直接测试时记忆表现并未变差。

questions.prompt: Why does the lecturer limit the practical conclusion?
options: Participants were not permitted to write their own plans.
The researchers measured only completed work.
All the puzzles involved personal obligations.
Brief voluntary puzzles differ from demanding real-life responsibilities.
questions.answer: Brief voluntary puzzles differ from demanding real-life responsibilities.
questions.explanation: 实验谜题短、自愿参加且没有考试截止压力，不能直接推广到困难的现实义务。
